contributions.statement: When a multi-step agent plan fails at one step, record each step's inputs, outputs and status and redo only the failed step and its downstream dependents (keeping the step's input/output interface fixed) instead of replanning the whole task.
contributions.evidence: §4.3, Fig. 4 ablation: removing minimal-subgraph repair costs about 6-8 points on Mistral-7B (ALFWorld 7.72, ScienceWorld 6.48) and similar on Llama-3-8B; figure only, single runs, 7-8B models, text-game environments, no code.
relative_to: workflow-engine retry of a failed task plus its downstream (Airflow/Make-style incremental re-execution)

contributions.statement: Have the model simulate a compiled plan (tool choice, dependencies, interfaces) before executing it and repair flagged steps first.
contributions.evidence: §5.3, Fig. 6: flags 19-27% of plans as risky with reported precision >74% (ground truth undefined); Fig. 4: removing it costs about 4-5 points on Mistral-7B.
relative_to: LLM self-critique / plan verification before acting (Self-Refine, plan-and-check)

reason: Localized subgraph repair adds only a weak magnitude (figure-only ablation, 7-8B models, text games) to a known checkpoint/re-execute practice, so it stays an open hypothesis. The headline DAG-vs-ReAct gains are unreleased, not compute-matched and not coding, and they cannot back a gate for a frontier-model Java team.
